turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

Looking at the training data, several clear device-physics trends emerge among the highest-efficiency (>16%) devices:

**1. ETL/perovskite interface passivation matters enormously.** The very top entries (24.8%, 21.33%, 20.0%, 19.7%) all share a *modified* fullerene interface (TmPyPB, [BMIM]BF4, Au-np, Choline chloride) — these reduce trap-state recombination at the ETL/perovskite interface and improve electron extraction/selectivity without adding series resistance.

**2. PTAA as HTL + Cu back contact is a reproducible high-performance recipe.** Multiple training rows with `C60 | BCP` (or `PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP`) / PTAA / Cu give 16.9–19.09%, versus the same stack with Ag or Al giving only 14–17%. Cu's work function/less reactive interface with PTAA appears to reduce back-contact recombination losses relative to Ag/Al in this specific HTL context.

**3. NiO-c bilayer/composite HTL engineering (NiO-c | NiO-mp, NiO-c | SYx) boosts hole selectivity** — seen at 17.4–18.4%, indicating better hole extraction/blocking of electron back-flow versus single-layer NiO-c.

**4. Custom donor-acceptor small-molecule ETL interlayers (ITCPTC-Th/Se, DBFMT, TTC) combined with proven C60|BCP or P3CT-Na/PTAA stacks reliably push efficiency into the 16–18.5% range** by improving energy-level alignment and suppressing interfacial recombination.

Matching these physics-informed patterns against the pool:

- **c097** (`ITCPTC-Se | C60 | BCP`, P3CT-Na, Ag) is essentially the *same architecture* as the 18.49% training champion (`ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP`, P3CT-Na, Ag) — only the chalcogen differs, so nearly identical band alignment/passivation behavior is expected.
- **c044** (`PCBM-60 | BCP`, PTAA, Cu) reproduces the PTAA+Cu combination that consistently yields 16.9–19.1% in training.
- **c051** (`PCBM-60 | BCP`, NiO-c | NiO-nw, Ag, double spin-coating) mirrors the NiO-c bilayer strategy (NiO-c|NiO-mp) that gave 18.4%.
- **c063** (`ITCPTC-Se | Rhodamine 101 | LiF`, P3CT-Na, Ag) closely tracks the analogous Th-based training entry (16.41%).
- **c085** (`TTC | C60 | BCP`, PTAA, Ag) leverages the strong, well-selective C60|BCP/PTAA/Ag base (14–17%) with an added interfacial dipole/passivation layer analogous to DBFMT’s boost to 18.16%.

These five candidates combine the strongest recurring signals: fullerene interface passivation, PTAA/Cu or NiO bilayer hole-selective contacts, and donor–acceptor interlayer engineering — the features most associated with the top quartile of training efficiencies.

Final: c097, c044, c051, c063, c085
